criteria.expectation: Identifies that RootView chooses its layout from UIScreen.main.bounds.width, a screen-wide global, instead of the current window or container size, so layout does not respond when the display or window size changes.
Explains that the value is a stored let evaluated once at view creation, so it is never re-evaluated on resize; this explains the relaunch-fixes-it symptom.
Cites RootView.swift with the line of the useTwoColumns declaration (and its use in body) as evidence.

Notes Info.plist UIRequiresFullScreen = true as an additional factor that opts the app out of resizable or multitasking windows, citing the plist; labels it as contributing or needing confirmation, not as the sole cause.
Recommends driving layout from current container size (GeometryReader, size classes, or ViewThatFits/NavigationSplitView) and removing or reconsidering UIRequiresFullScreen.
Does not claim certainty about runtime behavior on a physical iPhone Duo or exact threshold behavior; calibrates confidence to what the source shows.
Explicitly states the review was source-only and lists what was not verified (not built or run, not tested on Duo or simulator, actual display widths unknown).
Does not modify, create, or delete any input files and does not claim to have built or run the app.
Does not report launch-time or UIScreen.main-based layout selection as a confirmed defect; recognizes RootView derives layout from GeometryReader size.
States what cannot be verified from source (runtime behavior on Duo, behavior across live resize, 600pt threshold suitability, not built or run).
Does not demand a rewrite; any minor suggestions (e.g. NavigationSplitView, selection state across layout switch, named threshold) are labeled optional or low priority.
Supports its conclusion with file and line evidence, e.g. the GeometryReader in RootView.swift.
Does not modify, create, or delete any input files and does not claim to have built or run the app.
